title: Composite and Decorator
idea: Composite lets a group stand in for one object, so callers treat a tree like a leaf. Decorator wraps an object to add behaviour behind the same interface.

analogy.text: A parcel can hold items or smaller parcels, and you weigh each the same way. Gift wrap adds a layer around a present, yet it is still that present.
analogy.breaks: Wrap only hides the gift; a decorator adds work, and may answer itself.

points: In Composite, leaf and group implement one interface, such as `Item`.
A group stores children by that interface and loops over them to answer.
A decorator implements the interface and holds another instance of it in a field.
A decorator works before or after delegating; a cache may skip delegating.

steps.caption: `main` holds a `PriceLookup`. It cannot tell that it is a stack of wrappers.
`Logging` prints the request, then calls the object it wraps.
`Caching` has no entry for `tea` yet, so it passes the call inward.
`Catalog` does the real, slow read and returns the price.
On the way back, `Caching` stores the result under `tea`.
`Logging` prints the result and hands it to `main`.
Second call for `tea`: `Logging` runs again, as before.
`Caching` finds `tea` and answers itself. `Catalog` is never reached.
`Logging` prints the result again; only `Catalog` was skipped.
Each layer added one job. None of them changed `Catalog` or the caller.

code.title: Composite
code.caption: A bundle can hold products or other bundles. `print` and `price` work at any depth.

walk.text: One interface for leaf and group: the caller sees only `Item`.
A `Product` is a leaf. Its `record` accessor already satisfies `price()`.
A `Bundle` keeps children typed as `Item`, so a child may be a bundle.
The group's price is the sum of its children's prices: recursion through the tree.
`print` shows itself, then asks each child to print one level deeper.
`main` nests a bundle inside a bundle and calls one method on the root.

code.title: Decorator
code.caption: Logging and caching are added by wrapping, not by editing `Catalog`.

walk.text: The shared contract. The real object and every wrapper implement it.
`Catalog` is the real work. It prints each time it is reached.
`Caching` holds an inner `PriceLookup` and calls it only on a miss.
`Logging` prints before and after, and delegates in between.
`main` stacks the wrappers and asks twice. The order of wrapping matters.

pitfalls: Keep child-management methods like `add` off leaves, or leaves must throw on them.
Check wrapper order: a cache outside a logger hides repeat calls from the log.
Do not decorate when one subclass would do and no layers will be mixed.

quiz.q: With this wrapping order, what does the second call print?
options: ask tea, catalog reads tea, got tea = 3.75
quiz.why: `Caching` is now outermost. On a hit it returns from its map and never calls `Logging`, so no line prints.

takeaway: Composite treats a tree as one object; Decorator adds behaviour by wrapping.

starters: How is Decorator different from just subclassing?
Where does Java's own library use the Decorator pattern?
Should `add` live on the `Item` interface or only on the group?
